opennyai_summary.arguments:
In support, Ld. Addl. PP placed reliance on the   judgment of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Balraj Sharma V. State   (UT Chandigarh), 2016(1) FAC 16).
The appellant has pleaded that the minimum sentence   for misbranding as prescribed under Section 16(1)(a)PFA Act, is   imprisonment for a term of not less than six months; and therefore, 
 the Ld. MM could not have given a sentence of TRC i.e. less than   the minimum prescribed period of six months.
Even if the same is   treated as misbranding in view of the accused pleading guilty, it may   be mentioned that PFA Act stands repealed and has been replaced by   the Food Safety & Standards Act,2006 ("FSS Act" in short).
Under   FSS Act, misbranding is punishable only with fine and punishment   of imprisonment has been done away with.
Ld. Counsel placed reliance upon the judgment of Hon'ble High   Court of Delhi in State Govt of NCT of Delhi V. Jagdish Tyagi   2017 (2) FAC 521, in support.
It is noted that as per said report, total dye content was   found to be "13.16ppm" as against prescribed standard of not more   than "100ppm".
Considering that the food colour used was   permissible and was within the prescribed limit, Ld. MM found it to   be a case of 'misbranded'.
To which, the respondent pleaded guilty   and prayed for leniency.
